resources.string: Check a link for phishing and malware before you open it.
“%1$s:” links are not supported. Only http and https can be checked.
This does not look like a valid link.
This link is flagged as phishing or malware. Do not open it or enter any of your data.
The link shows suspicious signs. Be careful and verify the source.
Minor risk signs were found. Open it only if you trust the source.
The checked sources found no threats for this link.
Only the local check ran. Add API keys in Settings for a fuller result.
No API key set. Add it in Settings.
Invalid API key or no access
Request quota exceeded, try again later
%1$d of %2$d engines flagged it as malicious
The link will be sent to VirusTotal and visible to its community.
The local check found no suspicious signs.
This link was rated as risky. Opening it may harm your device or your data. Open it anyway?
The Google Safe Browsing API is for non-commercial use only. Commercial apps should use the Google Web Risk API.
Data is sent unencrypted; do not enter passwords.
IP address instead of a domain
Legitimate sites are rarely opened by IP address.
The domain may use letters from another alphabet, a trick to imitate well-known sites.
Alphabets such as Latin and Cyrillic are mixed: a sign of a fake domain.
Everything before “@” is ignored; the real site comes after it.
Long subdomain chains are used to hide the real domain.
Long links can hide the real address.
A short link hides the real destination. The app never opens the link itself; the final address is shown only if VirusTotal already has it.
This zone is often used for phishing and spam.
The domain contains a well-known brand name but is not its official site.
The link downloads an app file. Install apps only from the official store.
No threat source responded (no key or no internet). Clean local checks do not mean the link is safe.
The domain closely imitates a popular site (letter swaps, 0→o, 1→l, rn→m).
